## Read the Snakemake outputs

Replace the download and transformation chunks in your Module 2 report
with one of these language-specific examples. `datclean` and `summaries`
preserve the Module 2 names; `top10` and `subset` replace the
transformations previously performed inside the two plotting chunks.

For an R report:

``` r
datclean <- read.csv("work/1_names_clean.csv")
summaries <- read.csv("work/2_yearly_winners.csv")
top10 <- read.csv("work/3_top_names.csv")
subset <- read.csv("work/3_selected_names.csv")
```

For a Python report:

``` python
import pandas as pd

datclean = pd.read_csv("work/1_names_clean.csv")

summaries = pd.read_csv("work/2_yearly_winners.csv")
top10 = pd.read_csv("work/3_top_names.csv")
subset = pd.read_csv("work/3_selected_names.csv")
```

Use `summaries` for the table, `top10` for the top-names plot, and
`subset` for the names-over-time plot. These files have already been
transformed by the workflow, so do not repeat those transformations in
the report.

At minimum, adapt your report to:

-   replace the Module 2 download and transformation code with reads of
    the workflow-generated CSV files;
-   display `2_yearly_winners.csv` as the captioned table;
-   recreate the top-names and names-over-time plots from the prepared
    inputs, retaining their figure labels and cross-references;
-   include a value computed with inline code; and
-   report the R or Python environment used to render it.

After each edit, run:

``` bash
snakemake --cores 1
```

Then open `results/4_report.html`. When only this file changes,
Snakemake re-runs the report rule while leaving the upstream analysis
outputs untouched.
